# Plan a 3-day weekend trip with DeepSeek, based on your interests and budget

> **In short:** DeepSeek is a free AI assistant you can use in any browser. Give it a destination, your interests, and a rough budget, and it will draft a day-by-day weekend itinerary with activity ideas, food suggestions, and a cost breakdown — usually in under a minute. It can't book hotels or flights for you, but it's a strong starting point for planning.

You've got three days off, a vague idea of where you want to go, and zero interest in scrolling through forty travel blogs. DeepSeek (a free AI chatbot you can use through a web browser) can turn a few sentences about what you like and how much you want to spend into a draft itinerary you can actually use. This guide walks you through asking for that plan, refining it, and saving it somewhere handy.

## Before you start
- **A free DeepSeek account** — sign up with an email address at the official DeepSeek website. The free tier is enough for trip planning.
- **A web browser** on a phone or computer — DeepSeek works in Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge.
- **Rough answers to four questions**: where you want to go, when, what you enjoy (food? nature? museums? nightlife?), and a ballpark budget per person. Don't worry about being precise.
- **About 10–15 minutes** for your first try. The whole conversation, including tweaks, usually takes less time than a single packing list.

## Step 1 — Open DeepSeek and start a new chat
Go to the official DeepSeek website and sign in with the account you made. Once you're in, you'll see a clean chat screen with a text box at the bottom — this is where you type your request to the AI. There's usually a button like **"New Chat"** at the top-left or in the sidebar; tap it so the AI doesn't get confused by any previous conversation. If you don't see that button, refreshing the page works just as well — a blank chat box means you're starting fresh.

💬 Example: nothing to copy yet — this step is just opening the app.

You'll know it worked when the chat box is empty and ready for your first message.

## Step 2 — Send your first planning prompt
Tap inside the text box and type a clear request that covers destination, dates, interests, and budget. Press the **paper-airplane icon** (or hit Enter) to send it. The AI will pause for a few seconds while it thinks — this is normal — then a full itinerary will appear as a written reply. Don't worry if it isn't perfect on the first try; the whole point of the next steps is to improve it. If your screen shows a **Send** button instead of an airplane, that's the same thing.

💬 Example: "Plan a 3-day weekend trip to Lisbon, Portugal, for two adults in mid-October. We love walking neighborhoods, trying local food, and one nice museum. Budget is about €120 per person per day, not including flights. Give us a day-by-day plan with morning, afternoon, and evening ideas, plus rough costs."

You'll know it worked when the AI replies with a structured day-by-day plan, usually within 30–60 seconds.

## Step 3 — Read the itinerary and flag what you want to change
Read through the reply from top to bottom. Don't judge it too quickly — the first draft is a starting point, not the final answer. Look for the parts that genuinely excite you (jot those down) and the parts that feel off (an activity you'd never do, a restaurant type you don't eat, a cost that looks unrealistic). Use this quick mental checklist: Does each day have a sensible flow? Are travel times between spots reasonable? Is the food suggestion something you'd actually enjoy? This step is preparation for Step 4 — you're gathering feedback, not making changes yet.

💬 Example: none — this step is about reading, not typing.

You'll know it worked when you have a short mental list of "keep", "change", and "add" notes for the next message.

## Step 4 — Ask for specific changes in a follow-up message
Type a new message in the same chat, asking DeepSeek to revise based on your notes. The magic of an AI chat is that it remembers the whole conversation, so you can refer back to the earlier plan without re-explaining everything. Be specific about what you want — vague feedback like "make it better" usually produces a worse plan, while a clear ask like "swap the museum for an outdoor hike on Day 2" gets you exactly that. The reply will replace or update the earlier itinerary in the same chat window.

💬 Example: "That looks great overall. Three changes: please drop the fado show on Day 1 (we're too tired after the flight) and replace it with a relaxed waterfront walk. On Day 2, swap the museum for a half-day Sintra trip by train. Also push the dinner budget up a bit — we'd rather one great meal than three average ones."

You'll know it worked when the new reply reflects your changes and the rest of the plan still makes sense.

## Step 5 — Ask for a cost breakdown and packing reminders
Once the plan feels right, send one more message asking for a clear cost summary and a short packing list. This pulls everything into a format you can actually take on the trip. DeepSeek will usually reply with a table-style list of expected daily costs (accommodation, food, transport, activities) and a quick list of items to bring based on the weather and activities in your plan. If something in the breakdown looks too low or too high, ask it to adjust — that's why you keep chatting instead of starting over.

💬 Example: "Perfect. Now give me a cost breakdown per person per day (hotel, food, local transport, activities) and a short packing list for October weather and a lot of walking."

You'll know it worked when you see a tidy cost table and a packing list you can copy into your notes app.

## Step 6 — Copy the plan somewhere you can use it offline
Highlight the final itinerary with your mouse or finger, copy it, and paste it into your phone's notes app, email, or a shared document with your travel partner. AI chats can disappear if you clear your browser, and you don't want to be stuck at the airport with no internet trying to remember what Day 2 said. If you travel with someone, paste it into a shared note so you can both edit it in real time on the trip. Treat the AI's plan as a strong draft — still confirm opening hours and book restaurants yourself.

💬 Example: paste it into a note titled "Lisbon — Oct 17–19" and share it with your travel partner.

You'll know it worked when you can open the plan from your phone's home screen without signing into DeepSeek.

## Common mistakes
- **Too vague in the first message.** "Plan me a trip" gives generic answers. Always include destination, dates, who's going, and a budget number — even an approximate one.
- **Trying to make it perfect in one shot.** The first reply is rarely the best one. Plan on sending at least two follow-up messages to refine.
- **Trusting prices without checking.** AI cost estimates are reasonable guesses, not quotes. For anything expensive (tours, fancy restaurants), confirm the real price on the official website before you go.
- **Asking it to book things.** DeepSeek can plan, but it can't reserve hotels, buy tickets, or check your passport. You'll still do those steps yourself.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can draft a similar plan for a day trip, a long weekend, or even a "things to do this Saturday" list — the same prompt pattern works at any scale.
- **For your business or work:** The same skill (asking an AI to draft a structured plan from a few constraints) helps with meeting agendas, project outlines, and event planning.
- **If you're just getting started:** Treat the AI like a knowledgeable friend who talks fast — give it clear inputs, then edit the output. You'll get better results every time.

## Try it now
Open DeepSeek in your browser and send this exact message: *"Plan a 3-day weekend trip to a city I haven't visited yet. Pick one for me, suggest why, and give me a day-by-day plan with food ideas and a rough cost breakdown for two people on a mid-range budget."* See what it picks — then in your second message, ask it to swap one activity for something more outdoorsy. That's the whole loop, and it takes about three minutes.
